title: Tomato Leaf Spot
symptoms: The disease is characterized by small, circular spots with dark borders and gray to white centers. Black specks (fruiting bodies) may appear in the center of the spots. Lower leaves are usually affected first.
cause: Caused by the fungus Septoria lycopersici, which overwinter on infected plant debris and weeds.
prevention: Rotate crops annually. Remove and destroy infected plant debris. Avoid overhead watering. Use mulch to prevent soil splashing onto leaves.
organic_control: Apply copper-based fungicides. Remove infected lower leaves early in the season to reduce spread.
chemical_control: Fungicides containing chlorothalonil or mancozeb can be effective if applied early.
summary: Septoria leaf spot is one of the most common diseases of tomatoes and can cause significant foliage loss.

title: Rose Black Spot
symptoms: Circular black spots with feathery edges on leaves. Leaves turn yellow and drop prematurely.
cause: Fungal spores spread by water splash and wind in warm, humid conditions.
prevention: Plant resistant varieties. Ensure good air circulation. Keep foliage dry when watering.
organic_control: Neem oil or sulfur sprays. Remove all fallen leaves in autumn.
summary: The most serious fungal disease of roses worldwide, causing defoliation and weakening of the plant.

title: Citrus Canker
symptoms: Raised, corky lesions on leaves, stems, and fruit. Lesions often have a yellow halo.
cause: Bacterium entering through natural openings or wounds.
prevention: Decontamination of tools. Use of windbreaks to reduce wind-driven rain spread.
organic_control: Copper sprays can prevent infection but won't cure existing lesions.
chemical_control: Antibiotic sprays are rarely used in home gardens; focus is on prevention and copper sprays.
summary: A highly contagious bacterial disease that affects all types of citrus and can cause significant yield loss.
